title: Coordinate swap is an involution
statement: For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, swapping the two coordinates of every element twice returns the original set: writing $\mathrm{swap}(R) = \{(y,x) \mid (x,y) \in R\}$, one has $\mathrm{swap}(\mathrm{swap}(R)) = R$.
hypotheses_covered: R is an arbitrary subset of X × Y
replaced:
For any set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, applying $\texttt{swapInputSet}$ twice recovers
$R$: $\texttt{swapInputSet}(\texttt{swapInputSet}(R)) = R$.
